concept_checks.name: notebook and local tools
concept_checks.evidence: README lines 29–41; R.1; W.1 explains Notebook as prose plus executable cells, uv/Git, the kernel, and notebooks/01/1.1.ipynb.

concept_checks.name: dry run meaning and result boundary
concept_checks.evidence: README lines 58–65: prepare text, calculate predictions/cost/direction; no parameter update or weights; mode dry-run-no-weight-update and finite positive grad_norm.
concept_checks.reason: The command is introduced as a path check. Success is not equated with learning or new-question success. Detailed gradient mechanism is reasonably taught later, not needed merely to identify this check.

four_question_restatement.identity_and_role: This is an entry and project orientation page. It tells how to read first, then use a Notebook, and where later topics/products live.

why_mechanism_or_property.answer: ID figure previews a reversible character mapping; dry-run commands calculate a direction without applying an update. These two examples are not presented as trained ability.

why_need_or_use.answer: Readers need a first lesson and a way to distinguish reading, trying short code, checking a training path and using trained products; the page supplies those choices and boundaries.

four_question_restatement.use_inputs_outputs: Start at1.1 with the sentence, or install CPU Notebook tools for local experimentation. For the dry run, prepare toy text then inspect mode, loss and grad_norm.
four_question_restatement.example_evidence_and_limits: Figure shows repeated cat and dog keep IDs, and1.1 restores the sentence. Finite loss/gradient confirms a computable path only; no generalization or successful training follows.

unverified: No local installation, training, public-model download, GPU execution, Colab execution or scientific performance rerun was performed.
External upstream URLs and every README technical destination were not individually opened.
This is a README and necessary boundary continuity/layout review, not a full-book page-by-page reading or human learner test.
